A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCDD research, with matching authors, method, and retained experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training and evaluation results, including perplexity, correction-rate experiments, noise-schedule ablations, and zero-shot benchmark accuracy.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds LLM-judged text comparisons and controlled recovery experiments on corrupted OWT sequences.

M1.justification: The intended SCDD procedure remains unchanged: absorbing-mask and uniform corruption, Bayes-derived reverse transitions, discrete-time ELBO training, and ancestral parallel sampling. The new generator representation and correction experiments do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: LM1B, OWT, Wikitext-103, and the seven commonsense benchmarks are retained. v2 extends evaluation to corrupted-OWT reconstruction and exact token recovery, including a cross-ratio scenario that exposes GIDD+ to stronger corruption than its training schedule.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged: MDLM, ReMDM-cap, ReMDM-confidence, and GIDD/GIDD+ at the same noise ratios. The added judge comparisons reuse GIDD+; the theoretical comparison in new Table 1 introduces no newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces GPT-5.4 judging of 256 paired OWT reconstructions from identical inputs corrupted to t = 0.8, across six sampling budgets, using five quality criteria and winner selection. It also adds single-step recovery evaluation with 5, 10, 20, or 50 corrupted positions and touch/recovery metrics. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's correction counts and two noise-schedule ablations, v2 directly tests whether corrections restore original tokens and improve judged text quality. Matched-schedule and cross-ratio comparisons additionally examine correction quality under differing training-noise exposure. The original ablations remain intact.

E5.justification: v2 introduces paired t-tests for judge scores, binomial tests for win rates, and significance markers in Tables 4 and 9. Table 6 reports standard errors over 128 recovery samples. These substantially extend v1's averaging and Monte Carlo reporting; neither version documents repeated training seeds.

E6.justification: Existing perplexity, entropy, correction-rate, and zero-shot results are unchanged. New Tables 4 and 9 report SCDD win rates of 60.6% and 58.0% at 1024 steps, while GIDD+ scores higher on creativity. Table 6 adds 64.4%–69.4% exact recovery and a perplexity reduction from 154.8 to 25.5 at 50 corruptions; at five corruptions, perplexity instead rises from 22.0 to 23.8.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a matrix-generator consistency proposition and proof. Revised Proposition 10 corrects v1's misleading identification of SCDD with GIDD by explicitly identifying the alternative nonabsorbing kernel. There are also local formula corrections. Conversely, v2 drops the explicit non-mask support factor from Equations (7)–(8), although Appendix B retains it.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: independently controlled noise mechanisms, ELBO training with Bayes-derived sampling, and pretrained self-correction without remasking that improves parallel generation. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets exact recovery as evidence of meaningful correction, discusses GIDD+'s creativity advantage, and attributes cross-ratio weaknesses to lower training-noise exposure. Appendix E.3 expands the explanation that likelihood-based benchmark accuracy does not directly measure iterative generation or self-correction.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and the judge prompt in Figure 4. Appendix E.1 corrects the swapped arithmetic expressions underlying the LM1B and OWT token totals; the stated budgets, architecture, optimizer, and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al. (2025), Rojas et al. (2026), Sahoo et al. (2026), and Zheng et al. (2026), while removing the Bie et al. (2026)/LLaDA2.1 discussion. It sharpens the GIDD comparison in Appendix D.2 and new Table 1. ReMDM's citation update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and appendices A–G are retained. Changes include localized prose revisions, a reorganized GIDD proof, additional experimental subheadings, impact and acknowledgements sections, and removal of the contents page. Most existing exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the main text and references into a two-column conference layout, with reformatted equations and tables. It adds four tables and the judge-prompt figure. Existing Figures 2–3 use identical images but are separated and relocated; retained tables are renumbered and restyled.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's reliance on perplexity, edit counts, and illustrative samples, v2 provides more direct evidence that corrections recover content, alongside statistically assessed text-quality comparisons. The clarified GIDD proposition and added access information also help. Gains are tempered by reporting problems: Figure 4 does not specify pairwise winner selection, Appendix E.2 overstates significance relative to Table 9, and Equations (7)–(8) lose an explicit support factor.
